cells.tense: Right now you can let something end and keep what it grew.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: While a feeling is still raw, let it settle. Then settle one plain question about what it was owed and what is fair now. Keep the whole of it to yourself.
cells.core:
You can let a finished thing go and still keep what it grew. What you release leaves ground behind it, and that ground is the real gain. When feeling runs high, you weigh what is fair rather than what stings, and the people near you feel that hold without a word being said about it. Watch for the moment you sort a strong feeling into owed and done — that is the fitting move, and it keeps you standing on ground that does not shift under you.

Something is owed right now and you can see clearly what it is. Make that call yourself instead of letting the sting make it for you. Once it is made the heat drops, and whatever comes next has somewhere to stand.
cells.sheetLine: You can end something and keep what it grew.
cells.verb: releasing what has finished and turning it into ground for what comes next
cells.place: standing where a structure built on a false premise has just given way

cells.tense: You are bracing at a future you cannot write in yet.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: The next time someone close brings you a feeling, repair nothing and build nothing. Stay in it beside them for ten minutes, then hand it back.
cells.core:
Where endings are near, you're already building what comes after, and the building is outrunning the ending. You count what's owed and sort what stays before anything has actually finished, so the thing you're working on is still alive and doesn't get to be what it is. The attention is genuine. From the far side it reads as managing. Anyone across from you can tell you've moved on already.

When feeling arrives, it wants to be felt and not solved. Ten minutes of that, no plan attached, brings you back inside your own timing. You'll know what to do with it after. The doing can wait that long.
cells.sheetLine: You're counting the harvest before the season ends.
cells.verb: releasing what has finished and turning it into ground for what comes next
cells.place: standing where a structure built on a false premise has just given way

cells.tense: You are still at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: tend the fire without burning out
cells.ask: Go do one small act that belongs to what already ended — a call, a box, a walk by. Warmth first, no reckoning after it.
cells.core:
At its best this looks like letting a finished thing rest without carrying it around. You can name what's over, keep what it gave you, and put your weight down on ground that isn't still moving. Nothing dramatic in it — just someone who knows how to leave a room cleanly, and who trusts that the leaving was right even when it wasn't tidy.

Something has ended and you haven't stepped out of it yet. Nothing is being released, so what's finished keeps taking up room and the next thing has nowhere to land. The feeling is still there, it just isn't moving. You're not cold. You've gone quiet.

One act that belongs to what ended gives the fire something to do. That's all it is, not a reckoning. Warmth comes first; you don't have to decide anything about it.
cells.sheetLine: The door closed and you haven't stepped out of it.

cells.tense: The room around you is clearing and you haven't looked up from the desk.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Move a stuck thing today with a single act, before anyone agrees with it. Then look back and see what you did without waiting.
cells.core:
At its best, you make the call and things fall in line behind it. You know what needs to end and you end it, and the people near you find their footing on the ground you cleared. That kind of clearing has been happening here — something gave way, and you kept finding workable ground through it, over and over, without marking any of it as yours.

What's missing is your name on it. You've been treating the clear structure as if it were simply how things are, but you decided what stays and what goes, and you decided it more than once. The clearing isn't just the room. It's you.

One act today takes the shape of a decision you make and carry out before it's agreed to. Small, clear, done. The doing will show you what you've been doing silently.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing didn't happen to you. You did it.
